expired_orders_resident.checkpoint: before posting a valid limit order

claims.scope: POST_ONLY limit order posting against the per-side order cap in the limit order book

preconditions.text: _processLimitAskOrder() enforces a hard cap on the number of active ask orders per side (maxNumLimitsPerSide).; Expired limit orders remain resident in the ask book and are not filtered or removed before the capacity check.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.

safety.text: The per-side order cap should count only active, non-expired orders so that valid limit orders are not rejected due to expired orders occupying book space.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.

effects.text: Malicious actors could selectively deny participation for specific price ranges or actors because the expiration range is not checked at order posting.
effects.derivation: Program-generated direct negation witness for the selected safety pattern.

effect_coverage.reason: Program-generated exact coverage for selected direct impact.

assumptions: Posting limit orders is permissionless, so malicious actors can occupy book space with expired orders.
The per-side cap is reached by resident expired orders before a valid order is posted.
Expired orders can be created and left resident in the ask book.

limitations: The cap and expired-order occupancy are represented as grounded Boolean observables because the report gives no numeric cap value or order counts.
The attack ordering (occupy then post) is inferred from the griefing narrative rather than explicitly sequenced.
Only the censorship impact is formalized; other impacts are handled in separate passes.
